hero.lead: A city-state of 6.1 million that finances nationally significant infrastructure with long-dated green bonds: S$25.8 billion of public sector green bonds by March 2026, and a new 20-year green bond of S$2.6 billion in July.

register.name: Green SGS (Infrastructure), August 2046
register.detail: Monetary Authority of Singapore for the Government · new 20-year bond · priced 22 July 2026 · issued 3 August 2026 · coupon 2.375% · yield 2.40%
register.note: Placement orderbook of more than S$4.6 billion, 1.83 times the amount offered; S$50 million offered to individual investors
register.text: A new 20-year green bond of the Government of Singapore, a third tenor after the 50-year green bond of 2022 and the 30-year green bond of 2024, issued under the Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act 2021 and the Singapore Green Bond Framework. Its proceeds finance expenditures in support of the Singapore Green Plan 2030, including the Jurong Region Line and the Cross Island Line. It finances electric rail; no one of the seven standards is named.

register.name: HDB green notes due January 2030
register.detail: Housing & Development Board · issued 21 January 2025 · 5 years · coupon 3.120%
register.note: HDB had issued S$10.5 billion of green bonds, all for green buildings, by 31 March 2026
register.text: A green note of the Housing & Development Board, whose proceeds are used exclusively to finance or refinance eligible green projects in the Green Buildings category. The proceeds of HDB’s nine green bonds outstanding at 31 March 2025, S$8.455 billion in all, were fully allocated on a portfolio basis, with 98 eligible green projects on its register. It serves the shelter standard through public housing.

register.name: HDB green notes of 2024, four issues
register.detail: Housing & Development Board · S$800M due January 2029 at 2.977%, issued 23 January 2024 · S$800M due April 2027 at 3.409%, issued 30 April 2024 · S$965M due July 2026 at 3.244%, issued 23 July 2024 · S$900M due October 2028 at 2.757%, issued 30 October 2024
register.note: The S$965M note reached its maturity date on 23 July 2026
register.text: Four green notes of the Housing & Development Board issued in 2024, whose proceeds finance or refinance eligible green projects in the Green Buildings category. For its green bonds, HDB reports 22 projects certified BCA Green Mark GoldPlus, solar panels generating an estimated 3,618,000 kWh a year and an estimated 19,499,000 kg of CO2 saved a year. They serve the shelter standard through public housing.

register.name: PUB green notes due October 2031
register.detail: PUB, Singapore’s National Water Agency · issued 1 October 2024 · 7 years · coupon 2.502%
register.note: S$231.2 million, or 71%, allocated by 31 March 2025
register.text: A green note of PUB, Singapore’s National Water Agency, for sustainable water and wastewater management. By 31 March 2025, S$214.8 million had been allocated to the Tuas Water Reclamation Plant, with 800 million litres a day of used water treatment capacity, and S$16.4 million to Tuas NEWater Factory 1, with 25 million gallons a day of NEWater capacity. It serves the water standard and, through the treatment of used water, the shelter standard.

register.name: Green SGS (Infrastructure), June 2054
register.detail: Monetary Authority of Singapore for the Government · new 30-year bond by syndication · priced 21 May 2024 · issued 3 June 2024 · coupon 3.25% · yield 3.30%
register.note: Placement subscribed 2.45 times; reopened by auction for S$1.8bn in April 2025 and S$1.5bn in March 2026
register.text: The first 30-year Green Singapore Government Securities (Infrastructure) bond, sold by syndication with a public offer to individual investors, due 1 June 2054. Sovereign green bond proceeds finance the Jurong Region Line and the Cross Island Line, the only projects the Ministry of Finance names as meeting the criteria. It finances electric rail; no one of the seven standards is named.

register.name: PUB green bond due August 2052
register.detail: PUB, Singapore’s National Water Agency · issued 31 August 2022 · 30 years · coupon 3.433%
register.note: Issued in 2022; listed as an older instrument still outstanding
register.text: The first of PUB’s two green bonds reported to 31 March 2025, fully allocated: S$752.7 million to the Tuas Water Reclamation Plant and S$47.3 million to Tuas NEWater Factory 1. It serves the water standard and, through the treatment of used water, the shelter standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: A workforce of 6.1 million that runs one of the world’s great ports and financial centres.

items.name: The Green Bond Programme
items.label: Public sector green bonds, to March 2026
items.text: A sovereign curve of green bonds to 50 years: infrastructure financed across generations.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Nature reserves and park connectors across a fifth of a small island.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2018
items.text: Visitors already pay for the coast and the culture; their spending can finance what lasts.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: An island of little more than 700 square kilometres, much of it reclaimed from the sea.

items.name: S17 Community Kitchen
items.text: A social enterprise kitchen at Lengkok Bahru, among 1,200 rental flats, that serves the community through food, employment and care, with jobs for nearby residents and up to 500 meals a week for seniors.

items.name: The Straits Eye Centre
items.text: A business for impact that expands access to quality healthcare for elderly and vulnerable groups through a community-based, specialist-led care model, selected for DBS Foundation grant funding in March 2026.

items.name: InSchool
items.text: A business for impact that addresses gaps in after-school care for neurodivergent children with low-cost, structured programmes that build life skills and confidence, selected for DBS Foundation grant funding in March 2026.

items.name: Project Dignity
items.text: A social enterprise started in 2010 that runs Dignity Kitchen, Singapore’s first social enterprise food court, with a training centre for food and beverage skills and second-hand book shops, to return dignity to disadvantaged and disabled people through vocation.

items.name: The Social Space
items.text: A café, fair-trade shop and catering business that gives inclusive employment to incarcerated individuals, persons with disabilities and persons managing mental health conditions, with 12 beneficiaries in permanent roles in 2024.

items.name: Dajie Makan Place
items.text: A halal restaurant business with four outlets, in Bedok, Bukit Batok, Clementi and Yishun, that gives priority in hiring to persons with disabilities and ex-offenders.
